title: Model Memory vs Retrieval
goals: Explain the mechanism and terminology of retrieval and indexing
Apply the stated procedure to a new case with a traceable result

vocabulary: The collection of records available for a task
A searchable representation of that collection
Whether a record is current for the requested time

blocks.text: Index v1 contains notice N1 for room A. Corpus v2 supersedes it with N2 for room B, but the query still returns N1. What can be reported?
The stale index returns old evidence. It cannot establish current room approval; refresh against authorised corpus v2 or report unresolved freshness.

independent_case.title: Apply a new case independently
independent_case.task: Corpus has public P, teacher-only T and withdrawn W. A student search returns all three. Identify the filtering defect and whether hiding T after generation is sufficient.
independent_case.answer: Teacher explanation: Filter authorisation and active status before evidence reaches the student generation path: P only. Hiding a final citation does not undo exposed teacher content.
independent_case.source: primary source W4, first curriculum occurrence

misconceptions: The worked result establishes every future case
High retrieval similarity does not override permissions or make an obsolete source current.
A missing input may be replaced without recording the change
A replacement changes the evidence or contract. Record the change and its justification; do not silently turn unknown into a measured value.
Repeating an assessed case is new independent evidence
A replay checks consistency. An example used for feedback or revision cannot later be described as untouched final evaluation.

blocks.text: A closer explanation

Assign stable document IDs, versions and permitted access before indexing. Retrieve only authorised records. Preserve source references and define behaviour when a document is missing, outdated or access-restricted.
